if: a recipient has availed input tax credit on a supply
the supply is NOT one on which tax is payable on reverse charge basis
he fails to pay the supplier the value of supply together with the tax payable thereon within one hundred and eighty days from the date of issue of the invoice
then: CONFLICT — the two locally held sources state the consequence differently and this file resolves neither. Source A: an amount equal to the input tax credit availed is ADDED TO HIS OUTPUT TAX LIABILITY, along with interest thereon. Source B: that amount is PAID BY HIM ALONG WITH INTEREST PAYABLE UNDER SECTION 50
note: The one-hundred-and-eighty-day rule itself is common to both sources, as is its exclusion of reverse-charge supplies. Only the mechanism of the consequence differs. Source B carries a footnote recording the substitution by Act 8 of 2023 with effect from 1-10-2023, which is after the date of source A — but the resolution is a legal determination, not an extraction, and is left open here deliberately. The manner in both cases is 'as may be prescribed', so neither source closes the computation on its own.

evidence.section: CGST Act s.16(2), second proviso (source A, Act as updated 31-08-2021)
evidence.quote: Provided further that where a recipient fails to pay to the supplier of goods or services or both, other than the supplies on which tax is payable on reverse charge basis, the amount towards the value of supply along with tax payable thereon within a period of one hundred and eighty days from the date of issue of invoice by the supplier, an amount equal to the input tax credit availed by the recipient shall be added to his output tax liability, along with interest thereon, in such manner as may be prescribed:
